title: wordpress.org/openverse/: unauthenticated open redirect — `str_replace()`'s 4th arg is a count, not a limit; bypasses WordPress.org SSO allow-list
vulnerabilityInformation: A vulnerability was discovered in the open redirect feature of a WordPress theme that serves a subdirectory site. The vulnerability was caused by incorrect use of a string replacement function where the fourth argument, intended to limit replacements to one occurrence, was actually interpreted as an output parameter rather than a limit. This caused all instances of the path prefix to be removed instead of just the leading one. When a specially crafted path containing the prefix twice was requested, the remaining portion could be concatenated with a base URL in a way that altered the authority component, redirecting users to an attacker-controlled destination. The redirect used an unsafe API that performed no destination validation. The vulnerability allowed unauthenticated attackers to bypass the site's SSO redirect allow-list by crafting URLs that appeared to point to the legitimate domain but redirected elsewhere. The impact included silent redirection of users to attacker-controlled hosts with permanent browser caching and legitimate referrer information, creating an effective phishing vector.
